units.text: 10. The local administration decides to refuse support for an initiative project in one of the following cases:
units.label: Part 10 Art. 49

units.text: 1) failure to comply with the established procedure for submitting and considering the initiative project;
units.label: Point 1 Part 10 Art. 49

units.text: 2) the initiative project does not comply with federal laws and other regulatory legal acts of the Russian Federation, laws and other regulatory legal acts of constituent entities of the Russian Federation, or the municipal charter;
units.label: Point 2 Part 10 Art. 49

units.text: 3) the initiative project cannot be implemented because local self-government bodies lack the necessary powers and rights to exercise powers not assigned to local self-government bodies;
units.label: Point 3 Part 10 Art. 49

units.text: 4) insufficient local budget funds from sources other than initiative contributions to implement the initiative project;
units.label: Point 4 Part 10 Art. 49

units.text: 5) the problem described in the initiative project can be resolved more effectively by another means;
units.label: Point 5 Part 10 Art. 49

units.text: 6) the initiative project has been found not to have passed competitive selection.
units.label: Point 6 Part 10 Art. 49

units.text: 11. The local administration may, and in the case provided for in point 5 of part 10 of this Article must, propose that the project initiators jointly revise the initiative project, and recommend submitting it to the public authority competent to consider it.
units.label: Part 11 Art. 49

units.text: 12. The procedure for proposing, submitting, discussing and considering initiative projects, and for their competitive selection, is established by the municipal representative body.
units.label: Part 12 Art. 49

units.text: 13. For initiative projects proposed to obtain financial support through interbudgetary transfers from the budget of the constituent entity of the Russian Federation, the required contents of projects, the procedure for considering them, including grounds for refusing support, and the procedure and criteria for their competitive selection are established in accordance with a law and/or other regulatory legal act of the constituent entity. In that case, the requirements of parts 4, 9–12, 14 and 15 of this Article do not apply.
units.label: Part 13 Art. 49

units.text: 14. If several initiative projects are submitted to the local administration, including projects describing priority problems of similar substance, the local administration organizes competitive selection and informs the project initiators.
units.label: Part 14 Art. 49

units.text: 15. Competitive selection of initiative projects is entrusted to a collegial body (commission), whose formation and operating procedures are determined by a regulatory legal act of the municipal representative body. The local administration forms the membership of the collegial body (commission). Half of its total membership must be appointed on the basis of proposals from the municipal representative body. During competitive selection, project initiators and their representatives must be given the opportunity to participate in the collegial body’s (commission’s) consideration of initiative projects and to present their positions on them.
units.label: Part 15 Art. 49

units.text: 16. Project initiators, other citizens residing in the relevant municipality and authorized by a citizens’ assembly or meeting, and other persons specified by the legislation of the Russian Federation may exercise public oversight of implementation of an initiative project in forms that do not conflict with that legislation.
units.label: Part 16 Art. 49

units.text: 17. Information on the local administration’s consideration of an initiative project and on its implementation progress, including the use of funds and property and/or labor contributions by persons interested in its implementation, must be made public, including by posting it on the municipality’s official website on the Internet information and telecommunications network.
units.label: Part 17 Art. 49

units.text: 18. The local administration’s report on the outcomes of an initiative project must be made public, including by posting it on the municipality’s official website on the Internet information and telecommunications network, within 30 calendar days after completion of the project. In a rural settlement, the rural settlement elder may bring this information to citizens’ attention.
units.label: Part 18 Art. 49

units.text: Article 50. Territorial public self-government
units.label: Art. 50

units.text: 1. Territorial public self-government means citizens’ self-organization at their place of residence in part of a municipality’s territory to implement their own initiatives on matters directly ensuring the population’s daily life, independently and under their own responsibility.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 50

units.text: 2. The boundaries of the territory in which territorial public self-government is exercised are established by the municipal representative body on the proposal of the population residing in that territory.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 50

units.text: 3. Territorial public self-government is exercised directly by the population through citizens’ meetings (conferences), and also through the establishment of territorial public self-government bodies.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 50

units.text: 4. Territorial public self-government may be exercised within the following residential territories: an apartment building, a group of residential buildings, a residential neighborhood, a rural settlement or other residential territories. Each such residential territory may belong to only one territorial public self-government organization.
units.label: Part 4 Art. 50

units.text: 5. Territorial public self-government bodies are elected at meetings (conferences) of citizens residing in the relevant territory.
units.label: Part 5 Art. 50

units.text: 6. Territorial public self-government is deemed established from the moment its charter is registered by the authorized local self-government body of the relevant municipality. The procedure for registering the charter of territorial public self-government is determined by regulatory legal acts of the municipal representative body.
units.label: Part 6 Art. 50

units.text: 7. In accordance with its charter, a territorial public self-government organization may be a legal entity and is subject to state registration in the organizational and legal form of a nonprofit organization.
units.label: Part 7 Art. 50

units.text: 8. A citizens’ meeting on the organization and exercise of territorial public self-government is quorate if at least one third of the residents of the relevant territory aged eighteen or over participate.
units.label: Part 8 Art. 50

units.text: 9. In the cases provided for by the municipal charter and/or regulatory legal acts of the municipal representative body and the charter of territorial public self-government, a citizens’ meeting’s powers may be exercised by a citizens’ conference (a meeting of delegates). The procedure for calling and holding a citizens’ conference (meeting of delegates) and electing delegates is determined by the municipal charter and/or regulatory legal acts of the municipal representative body and the charter of territorial public self-government.
units.label: Part 9 Art. 50

units.text: 10. A citizens’ conference on the organization and exercise of territorial public self-government is quorate if at least two thirds of the delegates elected at citizens’ meetings participate, representing at least one third of the residents of the relevant territory aged eighteen or over.
units.label: Part 10 Art. 50

units.text: 11. The exclusive powers of a citizens’ meeting or conference exercising territorial public self-government include:
units.label: Part 11 Art. 50

units.text: 1) establishing the structure of territorial public self-government bodies;
units.label: Point 1 Part 11 Art. 50

units.text: 2) adopting the charter of territorial public self-government and amendments and additions to it;
units.label: Point 2 Part 11 Art. 50

units.text: 3) electing territorial public self-government bodies;
units.label: Point 3 Part 11 Art. 50

units.text: 4) determining the principal areas of activity of territorial public self-government;
units.label: Point 4 Part 11 Art. 50

units.text: 5) approving the revenue and expenditure estimate of territorial public self-government and the report on its execution;
units.label: Point 5 Part 11 Art. 50

units.text: 6) considering and approving reports on the activities of territorial public self-government bodies;
units.label: Point 6 Part 11 Art. 50

units.text: 7) discussing an initiative project and deciding whether to approve it.
units.label: Point 7 Part 11 Art. 50

units.text: 12. Territorial public self-government bodies:
units.label: Part 12 Art. 50

units.text: 1) act in the interests of the population residing in the relevant territory;
units.label: Point 1 Part 12 Art. 50

units.text: 2) may conduct economic activities for territorial improvement and upkeep and other economic activities aimed at meeting the social and everyday needs of citizens residing in the relevant territory, both using those citizens’ funds and under an agreement between territorial public self-government bodies and local self-government bodies using local budget funds;
units.label: Point 2 Part 12 Art. 50

units.text: 3) ensure implementation of other decisions adopted at citizens’ meetings and conferences on matters directly ensuring the population’s daily life in the relevant territory;
units.label: Point 3 Part 12 Art. 50

units.text: 4) may submit draft municipal legal acts to local self-government bodies; these drafts must be considered by those bodies and local self-government officials competent to adopt the acts.
units.label: Point 4 Part 12 Art. 50

units.text: 13. Territorial public self-government bodies may propose an initiative project as project initiators.
units.label: Part 13 Art. 50

units.text: 14. The charter of territorial public self-government establishes:
units.label: Part 14 Art. 50

units.text: 1) the territory in which it is exercised;
units.label: Point 1 Part 14 Art. 50

units.text: 2) the goals, tasks, forms and principal areas of activity of territorial public self-government;
units.label: Point 2 Part 14 Art. 50

units.text: 3) the procedure for forming territorial public self-government bodies and terminating their powers, their rights and duties, and their term of office;
units.label: Point 3 Part 14 Art. 50

units.text: 4) the decision-making procedure;
units.label: Point 4 Part 14 Art. 50

units.text: 5) the procedure for acquiring property and for using and disposing of that property and financial resources;
units.label: Point 5 Part 14 Art. 50

units.text: 6) the procedure for terminating the exercise of territorial public self-government.
units.label: Point 6 Part 14 Art. 50

units.text: 15. Local self-government bodies may not impose additional requirements on the charter of territorial public self-government.
units.label: Part 15 Art. 50

units.text: 16. In accordance with the procedure established by a law of the constituent entity of the Russian Federation, territorial public self-government organizations, including those operating without registration as legal entities, may receive support from budget appropriations of the constituent entity and local budgets.
units.label: Part 16 Art. 50

units.text: 17. The procedure for organizing and exercising territorial public self-government, and the conditions and procedure for allocating the necessary funds from the local budget, are determined by regulatory legal acts of the municipal representative body.
units.label: Part 17 Art. 50

units.text: Article 51. Rural settlement elder
units.label: Art. 51

units.text: 1. To organize interaction between local self-government bodies and residents of a rural settlement when resolving matters directly ensuring the population’s daily life, a rural settlement elder may be appointed in a rural settlement located within an urban okrug or municipal okrug.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 51

units.text: 2. A rural settlement elder is appointed by the representative body of the municipality that includes the rural settlement, upon nomination by a citizens’ meeting of that settlement. The elder is appointed from among citizens of the Russian Federation residing in the settlement and having the right to vote, and citizens of the Russian Federation aged eighteen or over on the date of nomination by the citizens’ meeting who own residential premises in that settlement.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 51

units.text: 3. The position of rural settlement elder is not a state office, state civil service position, municipal office or municipal service position. A rural settlement elder has no employment relationship or other directly related relationship with local self-government bodies.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 51

units.text: 4. A law of the constituent entity of the Russian Federation may establish another title for the position of rural settlement elder, taking into account historical and other local traditions.
units.label: Part 4 Art. 51

units.text: 5. A person may not be appointed as a rural settlement elder if the person:
units.label: Part 5 Art. 51

units.text: 1) holds a state office or state service position;
units.label: Point 1 Part 5 Art. 51

units.text: 2) has been declared legally incapable or of limited legal capacity by a court;
units.label: Point 2 Part 5 Art. 51

units.text: 3) has a conviction that has not expired or been expunged;
units.label: Point 3 Part 5 Art. 51

units.text: 4) has foreign agent status.
units.label: Point 4 Part 5 Art. 51

units.text: 6. A rural settlement elder’s term of office is established by the municipal charter and may not be shorter than two or longer than five years.
units.label: Part 6 Art. 51

units.text: 7. A rural settlement elder’s powers terminate early by decision of the representative body of the municipality that includes the settlement, upon a proposal of the settlement’s citizens’ meeting, and also in the cases established by points 1–7, 9 and 10 of part 1 of Article 30 of this Federal Law.
units.label: Part 7 Art. 51

units.text: 8. To perform the tasks assigned to them, a rural settlement elder:
units.label: Part 8 Art. 51

units.text: 1) interacts with local self-government bodies, municipal enterprises and institutions, and other organizations on matters directly ensuring the population’s daily life in the rural settlement;
units.label: Point 1 Part 8 Art. 51
